evidence.reason: fixer investigation: The finding's harm claim cannot be confirmed or refuted with the supplied evidence. The visible cmd_boot code (lines 1286-1305) already implements deliberate ownership gating: entered_boot prevents cleanup when another invocation holds run.lock, launched captures this invocation's pid/starttime for post-lock cleanup, and the comments state the fallback intent. Whether stop_owned_process(run, purge=False, launched=None) can actually stop another invocation's VM hinges on its fallback semantics (in-memory run dict vs re-reading run.json, and whether boot() records its own pid under the lock before any raise), and on cmd_run's structure including the cited lines 1408-1410 — none of which are present: the additional source is truncated at ~line 200 (qemu_command) and the region ends at 1342. Under the visible single-writer-lock design the recorded identity at cleanup time would be the caller's own launch, making the fallback appear safe; the alleged retry race requires stop-time re-reading of shared state that the truncated source does not establish. Relevant source evidence (stop_owned_process, boot, cmd_run) is missing, so unsure rather than valid or invalid.
